# 地持論義記

**Category:** 瑜伽部類
**Original Category:** 大小乘釋律部／大乘律疏
**Byline:** 隋 慧遠述
**Dynasty:** 隋
**Date:** 581–618
**Juans:** 3
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0704

## Contributors
- 慧遠 (A002000)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-fascicle exegetical commentary on the *Púsà dìchí jīng* ([KR6n0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0003), T30n1581) — Dharmakṣema's translation of the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* — composed by [淨影慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B7%A8%E5%BD%B1%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (Jìngyǐng Huìyuǎn, 523–592), the great Suí *Dìlùn* 地論 school master. Often referred to in catalogues simply by the alternative title 地持論 *Dìchí lùn*, conflating the *jīng* (sūtra) and *lùn* (treatise) titles. Survives in the *Xuzangjing* (X39n0704) and is one of the most important pre-Xuánzàng exegetical witnesses to the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* tradition in China.

**Abstract**

[淨影慧遠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B7%A8%E5%BD%B1%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) (also known as 大遠 *Dàyuǎn* or 隋遠 *Suíyuǎn*; not to be confused with the earlier 廬山慧遠 of Mt Lú) was the principal heir to the Northern *Dìlùn* school of Fǎshàng 法上 (495–580) and the most important systematic Buddhist scholar of the Sui imperial period. The *Dìchí lùn yìjì* is one of his major doctrinal commentaries, alongside the *Dà chéng yì zhāng* 大乘義章 (T1851 = [KR6n0122](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0122)). The dating bracket adopted (580–592) covers his late-life commentarial activity at the Jìngyǐngsì 淨影寺 in Cháng'ān after the death of his master Fǎshàng.

The commentary reads the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* through the lens of the *Dìlùn* school's *tathāgatagarbha*-influenced Yogācāra. It is repeatedly cited by the early Tang Cí'ēn commentators including [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) in [KR6n0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0008) *Yúqié shī dì lùn lüèzuǎn*, who treats Huìyuǎn's reading of the *Púsàjiè* (bodhisattva-precepts) section as a key scholastic precedent — even where Cí'ēn doctrine ultimately diverges from the *Dìlùn* tradition.

The work is also the principal pre-Xuánzàng Chinese commentary on the bodhisattva-precepts of the *Bodhisattvabhūmi*, and as such occupies an important place in the textual genealogy of the East Asian *Púsàjiè* tradition.
